decisions.decision: Complete Phase 4 Security, Performance, and AI Optimization Implementation for Single-User Deployment
decisions.rationale: Successfully implement Phase 4 core systems including security middleware, connection monitoring, response caching, performance tracking, and local AI optimization. Optimize for single-user deployment while maintaining family deployment readiness. Rate limiting disabled for personal use but architecture supports re-enabling for family sharing.
alternatives_considered: Continue with rate limiting enabled - would restrict single-user usage unnecessarily
Skip AI optimization - would miss performance improvements and model selection benefits
Delay implementation until family deployment - would delay immediate benefits
Implement full multi-user features now - would add complexity not needed yet
decisions.chosen_approach: Implement all Phase 4 systems with single-user optimization, disable rate limiting for personal use, maintain family deployment readiness

security_middleware.status: Complete - Rate limiting disabled for single-user
security_middleware.features: Rate limiting, input validation, request protection
security_middleware.family_ready: Rate limiting can be re-enabled when needed

connection_monitor.features: Health checks, graceful fallbacks, background monitoring

performance_tracker.features: Request tracking, system monitoring, performance analytics

local_ai_optimization.features: Query analysis, model selection, performance profiling

explicitly_omitted: Full multi-user authentication - not needed for single-user deployment
Complex rate limiting rules - simple enable/disable sufficient
Advanced caching strategies - basic caching provides good foundation
Comprehensive user analytics - privacy-focused approach preferred

expected_impact.performance: AI optimization improving model selection and response quality
expected_impact.reliability: Health monitoring and graceful fallbacks ensuring stability
expected_impact.security: Protection framework ready for family deployment
expected_impact.scalability: Architecture designed for multi-user scaling when needed

Test multiple requests without rate limiting - ✅ Working
Confirm family deployment readiness - ✅ Architecture ready

decisions.decision: Configure Claude Desktop with MCP filesystem server for direct FAITHH project access
decisions.rationale: Enable Claude Desktop to read FAITHH project files directly without manual context pasting. This bridges Claude Desktop (Windows) to the FAITHH project (WSL2) using MCP filesystem server, making the living workspace truly accessible from Jonathan's primary Claude interface.
alternatives_considered: Continue manual context pasting - tedious, error-prone, snapshot-based
Windows UNC path approach - simpler but less reliable, path breaks if WSL2 distro changes
Install Node.js on Windows - additional complexity, diverges from WSL2-native workflow
Add memory MCP server - redundant with FAITHH's existing memory architecture
decisions.chosen_approach: WSL2 Approach B using `wsl -e npx` command for filesystem server access

filesystem_server.security: Matches tool_policies.json restrictions, blocks ~/.ssh and .env files

sequential_thinking_server.purpose: Complex reasoning tasks for architectural discussions

explicitly_omitted.memory_mcp_server: FAITHH already has comprehensive memory architecture (faithh_memory.json, decisions_log.json, project_states.json, scaffolding_state.json). Adding separate memory layer would create coherence drift and undermine the Coherence Arbiter's validation system.
explicitly_omitted.cursor_mcp_servers: Context7, IDE Browser are specific to Cursor/VS Code integration, not needed for Claude Desktop's primary use case of file access.

decisions.expected_impact: Claude Desktop sessions become truly stateful - Claude can read CONTEXT.md, project_states.json, decisions_log.json directly. Eliminates manual pasting, enables live file access, completes the bridge between Claude Desktop and living FAITHH workspace.
decisions.verification: Test with questions: 'Read CONTEXT.md and tell me what project I'm working on' and 'What are my open loops in scaffolding_state.json?'

decisions.decision: Implement Phase 2 anchor validation for ground truth claim verification
decisions.rationale: Add ground truth validation of canonical state file claims against actual system behavior. This provides reality-check validation for the Coherence Arbiter's semantic convergence measurements, ensuring that documented claims reflect actual system capabilities.
decisions.implementation: AnchorValidator class in backend/anchor_validator.py with dependency injection pattern. Validates FAITHH project phase status against ML chips, ChromaDB scale, and PULSE engine capabilities. Integrated into CoherenceArbiter with 0.7 validity threshold.
key_insights: Dependency injection eliminates circular imports between backend, arbiter, and validator
Partial scoring handles API limitations gracefully (ChromaDB count endpoint unimplemented)
Anchor validation only fires with rag_chip_alignment (document-based queries)
0.825 score accurately reflects current system state, not inflated
Known limitation: Conversation-based RAG queries don't trigger anchor validation
infrastructure_issues: ChromaDB v1/v2 API endpoint changes require documentation and future resolution
Count API returns 410/501, requiring heartbeat proxy workaround

decisions.decision: Phase 3 Coherence Arbiter: UI surfacing, anchor expansion, behavior hints, tests
decisions.rationale: Surface coherence in the UI so users see when FAITHH is operating from strong vs weak ground; expand anchor validation with conservative checks; add advisory low-coherence hints without changing model output; protect behavior with tests.
alternatives_considered: UI-only (no anchor expansion) - deferred deeper validation
Behavior changes on low coherence (e.g. block reply) - rejected; advisory only
decisions.implementation: Backend: _enrich_phase3_metadata() adds tier, reasons, low_confidence, suggested_behavior to every coherence result. Anchor validator: two new evidence checks (default_provider_decision, pulse_documented) with weights 7.5% each; ML/Chroma/PULSE reweighted to 30/30/25. UI: coherence indicator (high/medium/low) and low-coherence hint in faithh_pet_v4.html. Tests: tests/test_coherence_arbiter_phase3.py. Docs: SYSTEM_OVERVIEW Coherence Arbiter section, docs/guides/COHERENCE_SIGNAL.md.
key_points: Tier and behavior hints are advisory only; no change to LLM output
Anchor expansion fails gracefully when decisions_log or state missing
Indicator only shown for non-streaming responses when coherence metadata present

decisions.decision: Implement Coherence Arbiter for RAG-Chip convergence measurement
decisions.rationale: Enable semantic convergence measurement between RAG retrieval and ML chip routing signals to provide quantitative coherence scoring. This addresses the need to measure how well the two modalities align, improving context routing quality and providing visibility into system behavior.
alternatives_considered: Signal strength only scoring (simpler but less meaningful)
Separate RAG and chip quality scores (no convergence measurement)
Full embedding space alignment analysis (computationally expensive)
Statistical correlation analysis (requires more data collection)
decisions.implementation: CoherenceArbiter class in backend/coherence_arbiter.py with cosine similarity convergence matrix calculation (np.mean(np.max(convergence_matrix, axis=1))) and signal strength weighting. Integrated into build_integrated_context() with 100ms timeout and graceful fallback.
decisions.next_phase: Phase 2: Anchor validation and adaptive thresholding
key_insights: Conversation-based RAG results (focused queries) appropriately fall back to signal strength as they lack document embeddings
Document-based RAG results (broad queries) achieve full convergence calculation with rag_chip_alignment signals
Score ordering shows meaningful differentiation between query types

decisions.decision: 2% weekly Astris decay rate
decisions.rationale: Balance between encouraging ongoing participation and not punishing temporary absence. 2% allows someone to take a month off without catastrophic decay, but still incentivizes regular engagement.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Too harsh - people would lose significant Astris after short breaks
Too lenient - doesn't meaningfully encourage participation
Could lead to hoarding and disconnect between current contribution and voting power

decisions.impact: Affects token distribution fairness and participation incentives

decisions.decision: 5% quarterly Auctor decay
decisions.rationale: Auctor represents civic voice/equality, so decay should be gentler than merit-based Astris. Quarterly decay ensures people who move away or become inactive don't retain permanent voting power, but allows for life circumstances.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Too frequent for a civic voice token - people have other responsibilities
Could lead to ghost voters who no longer participate in community

decisions.impact: Maintains fairness in civic voice while respecting life circumstances

decisions.decision: Use ChromaDB with 768-dim embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2)
decisions.rationale: Needed vector database for semantic search. ChromaDB offers good balance of features, performance, and ease of use. 768-dim model (all-mpnet-base-v2) provides good semantic understanding without excessive compute requirements.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Cloud-only, monthly costs, vendor lock-in
More complex setup, heavier resource requirements
Lower quality semantic search, harder to capture nuance

decisions.impact: Foundation for all RAG functionality, affects search quality
decisions.superseded_reason: Switched to 384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for faster inference and proper chunking

decisions.decision: Three-tier memory system (hot/warm/cold)
decisions.rationale: Mimics CPU cache hierarchy - different access patterns need different storage. Hot (current session) in RAM for speed, warm (user profile) in JSON for simplicity, cold (all history) in ChromaDB for semantic search.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Would be slow for frequently accessed data like user profile
Can't do semantic search, would grow too large
Adds complexity, doesn't solve semantic search problem

decisions.impact: Defines how FAITHH stores and retrieves all information

decisions.decision: FAITHH is a thought partner, not just a search tool
decisions.rationale: Jonathan's core problem is maintaining project coherence when attention shifts. He doesn't need another search engine - he needs a system that remembers WHY projects matter and helps him pick up where he left off. This fundamentally changes development priorities from accuracy-first to synthesis-first.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Would be impressive but wouldn't solve the actual problem of losing context when switching projects
Jonathan doesn't need more task lists - he needs to understand the 'why' behind tasks

decisions.impact: Changes success metric from 'accurate answers' to 'maintains coherence across attention shifts'. Focus shifts to Level 3 synthesis, not just Level 1 recall.

decisions.decision: Reindex ChromaDB with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim) and 1500-char chunking
decisions.rationale: Previous index used all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim) with inconsistent chunking. Switched to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for faster inference and proper 1500-char chunks with 200-char overlap for better semantic boundaries. Reduced from 93,533 docs to 32,499 well-structured chunks.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Slower inference, marginal quality improvement for this use case
Would lose too much context per chunk, hurting semantic search quality

decisions.impact: Cleaner, faster RAG search. 306 conversations (208 ChatGPT + 98 Claude) properly indexed.

decisions.decision: Deploy 12 Docker services on Gen8 MicroServer
decisions.rationale: Centralize infrastructure services on dedicated server. Gen8 has low power draw, ECC RAM, and 842GB free disk. Services include ChromaDB, Grafana, Prometheus, Gitea, Vaultwarden, Pi-hole, Docker Registry, Uptime Kuma, GitLab Runner, Node Exporter.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Desktop isn't always on; services need 24/7 availability
Monthly costs, data sovereignty concerns, already have hardware

decisions.impact: Reliable 24/7 infrastructure backbone. All services accessible via Tailscale.

decisions.decision: Build context injection system (generate_context.py → CONTEXT.md)
decisions.rationale: Need a single document any AI can consume for instant orientation. Source files are scattered (project_states.json, faithh_memory.json, decisions_log.json, etc.). Generation script reads all sources and produces a unified, regenerable CONTEXT.md plus immutable framing snapshots.

alternatives_considered.option: Manually maintain a single context doc
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Would go stale immediately — Jonathan's ADHD means manual upkeep won't happen consistently

alternatives_considered.option: Use RAG to answer context questions dynamically
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Too slow for session initialization; need instant orientation, not search

decisions.impact: Any AI session can be bootstrapped with CONTEXT.md. Framing snapshots capture understanding at key moments.

decisions.decision: Set Groq (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) as default LLM provider
decisions.rationale: Ollama local models were unavailable (systemd service was disabled). Groq provides fast, high-quality responses via API with free tier. Set as default so FAITHH works immediately; local Ollama available as fallback/override.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Models need to be loaded; adds friction to startup
API key may expire; Groq has been more reliable

decisions.impact: FAITHH starts working immediately without local model setup. ~2s response times via Groq.

decisions.decision: Broaden chip activation to fire on general project and business queries
decisions.rationale: Project_state chip only fired for 'what's next' queries (is_next_action_query). Natural questions like 'what projects am I working on?' fell through. Added is_project_query intent pattern and broadened project_state chip to fire on project OR business queries.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Would waste token budget on irrelevant queries
ML pipeline not yet built; need working system now

decisions.impact: Project queries now return structured data from project_states.json instead of only RAG fragments.

decisions.decision: Build PULSE Reflection Engine — tiered ML self-reflection protocol
decisions.rationale: FAITHH needs to evolve from reactive to proactive. ML-driven staleness detection, decision divergence tracking, and branch exploration give FAITHH autonomous self-awareness. Tier 1 runs on CPU in 11 seconds. Tiers 2-3 use RTX 3090 with local LLM. Dual-GPU setup allows ML to run while gaming on 1080 Ti.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Won't happen consistently — ADHD means manual upkeep falls off
Already have RTX 3090 locally; no need for cloud costs or data sovereignty issues
Tier 1 builds the embedding infrastructure Tier 2 needs, and gives immediate tangible results

decisions.impact: Foundation for FAITHH autonomous personality — scheduled sweeps, proactive notifications, avatar reactions based on system health.

decisions.decision: Set qwen25-grounded:latest as default model
decisions.rationale: The 14B Qwen 2.5 grounded model provides better reasoning and grounding capabilities than the 8B Llama model. After fixing the chat template conflict, it's ready for production use.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: 8B model has less capability for complex reasoning
Cloud dependency, not grounded

decisions.impact: All FAITHH queries will now use the more capable 14B grounded model by default

decisions.decision: Fix qwen25-grounded chat template conflict
decisions.rationale: The model was producing nonsensical responses due to Qwen's default system prompt overriding FAITHH's prompt. Adding explicit TEMPLATE directive to Modelfile resolved this.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Training was successful, issue was deployment configuration
q4_k_m quantization was fine, issue was template

decisions.impact: qwen25-grounded now works correctly and provides grounded responses

decisions.decision: Proceed with Qwen 2.5 14B grounding fine-tune
decisions.rationale: 14B model should provide better reasoning than 8B llama31. Expanded training data to 1914 examples across 16 categories for comprehensive grounding.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Limited capacity for complex queries
RTX 3090 can't handle 70B QLoRA efficiently

decisions.impact: More capable grounded model for FAITHH responses

decisions.decision: Never load SentenceTransformer in WSL scripts — use ChromaDB default embedding or route through backend
decisions.rationale: Loading SentenceTransformer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) in a WSL script triggers PyTorch CUDA initialization against the GTX 1080 Ti (sm_61 architecture). This causes catastrophic WSL memory pressure and crashes the entire WSL instance. The backend already has the model loaded lazily on CPU — use that instead. ChromaDB also supports default embedding functions that sidestep the issue entirely.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Tried and still crashes — PyTorch CUDA init happens before the env var takes effect in some load paths
Also triggers CUDA init on import of torch — the crash is at import time, not inference time

decisions.impact: All future indexer scripts must avoid importing sentence_transformers or torch directly. Use: (1) route through running FAITHH backend's /api/rag_search or embed endpoint, or (2) use ChromaDB collection.upsert() without embeddings and let the collection's default function handle it.
